date: 约公元前8世纪（传统年代）

title.zh: 塔洛斯：古典神话中的铜制守卫
title.en: Talos: The Bronze Guardian of Classical Myth

description.zh: 塔洛斯是古典神话中守卫克里特岛的巨大铜制自动体。现存古典文本中最清楚的塔洛斯叙事见于阿波罗尼奥斯·罗迪乌斯《阿尔戈英雄纪》；本事件把它作为早期人工生命与自动体想象来呈现，而不宣称它是现代人工智能的直接先例。
description.en: Talos is a giant bronze automaton who guards Crete in classical myth. The clearest surviving classical narrative appears in Apollonius Rhodius's Argonautica; this event presents Talos as an early imagination of artificial life and automata, without claiming him as a direct precursor of modern AI.

notes.zh: 原清单标题将塔洛斯归于《伊利亚特》，本事件已改用可核验的《阿尔戈英雄纪》叙事；加入 storyline 前需完成古典文献复核。
notes.en: The source list attributes Talos to the Iliad; this event uses the verifiable Argonautica narrative. Complete classical-text review before adding it to the storyline.

displayTitle.zh: 塔洛斯：古典神话中的铜制守卫
displayTitle.en: Talos: The Bronze Guardian of Classical Myth

displaySummary.zh: 从神话中的自动体，追问人工生命意味着什么
displaySummary.en: An automaton in myth raises an early question about artificial life

displayDescription.zh:
古典神话把塔洛斯描绘成守卫克里特岛的铜制巨人：他能够移动、巡逻，并以体内唯一的生命之血维持行动。这个形象把金属身体、自动运动和脆弱的生命核心组合在一起，成为西方文化中很早的人工生命想象之一。

现存最完整的古典叙事来自阿波罗尼奥斯·罗迪乌斯《阿尔戈英雄纪》第四卷，后世神话汇编又发展了他的守卫与死亡故事。它与现代 AI 没有直接技术谱系，却帮助观众理解人类为何不断用神话、文学和艺术想象“被制造的行动者”。
displayDescription.en:
Classical myth describes Talos as a bronze giant guarding Crete. He can move and patrol, yet depends on a single vulnerable life-fluid running through his metal body. The combination of an artificial body, autonomous motion and a fragile life core makes him an early Western imagining of artificial life.

The fullest surviving classical narrative appears in Book 4 of Apollonius Rhodius's Argonautica, while later mythographers developed his guard duty and death. Talos has no direct technical lineage to modern AI, but he helps show why people repeatedly imagine manufactured agents through myth, literature and art.

usage.zh: 塔洛斯古典文本的主要档案来源
usage.en: Primary archive source for the classical Talos episode

html.zh: 塔洛斯属于希腊神话中关于赫菲斯托斯造物、铜制身体和守卫者的叙事传统。现存较完整的塔洛斯情节来自阿波罗尼奥斯·罗迪乌斯的《阿尔戈英雄纪》，这一文本为我们理解塔洛斯的自动体形象提供了主要依据。
html.en: Talos belongs to a Greek mythic tradition of Hephaestus's creations, bronze bodies and artificial guardians. The fullest surviving Talos episode comes from Apollonius Rhodius's Argonautica, which provides the main textual basis for understanding Talos as an automaton.

html.zh: 塔洛斯把自动运动、人工身体和生命脆弱性放在同一个形象中，提出了“被制造的身体能否成为行动者”的早期想象。它不是现代 AI 的技术起点，却为后来关于机器人、人工生命和造物责任的叙事提供了文化母题。
html.en: Talos combines autonomous motion, an artificial body and vulnerable life in one figure, offering an early imagination of whether a manufactured body can become an agent. He is not a technical starting point for modern AI, but the myth supplies a cultural motif later reused in stories about robots, artificial life and creator responsibility.

html.zh: 古典学与机器人史研究者通常把塔洛斯视为自动体和人工生命想象的重要早期案例，但不会把它等同于现代 AI。它的长期价值在于让观众看到，关于人造身体、自动守卫和生命边界的疑问，早于计算机技术存在了数千年。
html.en: Scholars of classical myth and robotics history generally treat Talos as an important early case of automaton and artificial-life imagination, not as modern AI itself. His lasting value is to show that questions about manufactured bodies, autonomous guardians and the boundary of life predate computing by millennia.
